commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Cast Admiral Brass, Unsinkable ({2}{U}{B}{R}); its ETB mills four. Fill the graveyard with Pirates (Entomb, Buried Alive, Faithless Looting, Mary Read and Anne Bonny, Malcolm, channel/discard), then every beginning of combat on our turn return a Pirate creature card as a hasty base-4/4 with a finality counter. Prefer Pirates whose ETB/attack triggers do work regardless of base stats (Hostage Taker, Amphin Mutineer, Coercive Recruiter, Kitesail Larcenist, Jhoira, Zara, Port Razer). Roaming Throne naming Pirate doubles the Brass trigger and the returned Pirates' triggers; Power Conduit removes finality counters at instant speed so Pirates return to the graveyard for reuse; Port Razer and Timestream Navigator add combats/turns, each with another Brass trigger.
protected_core: Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 — Optimized: six Game Changers (Ancient Tomb, Cyclonic Rift, Demonic Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Jeska's Will, Vampiric Tutor), fast reanimation and tutors, but no deterministic two-card infinite identified; not cEDH.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Keep the list a Pirate-tribal graveyard-recursion deck: every add is a Pirate creature with ETB/attack value Brass can recur; reject generic reanimator payloads (Maskwood Nexus, non-Pirate fatties) and generic goodstuff (Rhystic-style taxes, Herald's Horn).

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Reviewed all 99: 31 lands + Brass's Tunnel-Grinder MDFC (land back face); 8 mana rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, 3 Signets, 3 Talismans); 30 Pirate/creature slots including Wonder; 8 graveyard/reanimation (Animate Dead, Buried Alive, Entomb, Faithless Looting, Living Death, Patriarch's Bidding, Reanimate, Victimize); tutors/draw (Demonic, Vampiric, Jeska's Will, Kindred Discovery, Black Market Connections); 10 interaction/protection pieces; engines Power Conduit, Roaming Throne, Shared Animosity. Overlap: Treasure ramp is over-supplied by low-impact two-drops (Scallywag) while repeatable removal-on-ETB and extra-turn effects were under-supplied.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: 31 lands + MDFC + 8 rocks + Treasure makers supports a turn-4 Brass with Sol Ring/rock. Colorless lands: Ancient Tomb, Cavern of Souls (Pirate any-color), Path/Orchard/Tower/Confluence fixers. Swaps keep the curve flat: removes a 1, three 2s and a 4; adds a 1, two 2s, a 3 and a 6 (Jhoira, a reanimation target rather than a hard-cast plan). Land count and fixing unchanged; colored demand shifts toward blue (adds three single-U cards, cuts four single-B cards), which the U sources (Signets, Talismans, Cavern, fixers) absorb.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Counterspell, Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, Siren Stormtamer; removal: Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Deadly Rollick, Feed the Swarm, Hostage Taker, Amphin Mutineer, Merchant Raiders channel, Otawara, Toxic Deluge; adds Kitesail Larcenist (one permanent per opponent, repeatable via Brass) and Warkite Marauder (per-attack neutralization). Graveyard hate (Bojuka Bog, Rest in Peace) is the main weakness; the list keeps castable Pirates, Kindred Discovery and Breeches/Ramirez card flow as a non-graveyard plan.

weakest_slots.weakness: Two-mana conditional Treasure only on turns we descended; as a Brass return it is a vanilla 4/4 haste with a weak end-step clause.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Lowest-impact Pirate: no ETB, no attack trigger, no protection; ramp role is duplicated by Lannery, Corsair Captain, Gemcutter, Malcolm Navigator, Ramirez and Black Market Connections.

weakest_slots.weakness: Can't block; explore only on Pirate damage; a 2-drop evasive body with marginal value as a Brass target.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Explore is small card selection; the slot is better spent on a two-drop that converts Brass's haste into an extra turn (another Brass trigger).

weakest_slots.weakness: Attack trigger costs {2} for a 2/2 token and needs another nontoken Pirate; mana-hungry and slow in multiplayer.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Same mana slot; Warkite's free attack trigger neutralizes the best blocker every combat and doubles under Roaming Throne.

weakest_slots.weakness: 1-drop that cannot block; as a Brass return it is a 4/4 unblockable haste body with no other value.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Ragavan is the stronger one-drop Pirate: Treasure accelerates the five-mana commander and each hit is card advantage; dash gives late-game haste even without Brass.

weakest_slots.weakness: Its death trigger is disabled for every Brass-returned Pirate because finality counters exile instead of dying; mainly fuels Victimize/Bombardiers/encore tokens.
weakest_slots.reasoning: A four-mana card whose payoff is anti-synergistic with the commander's main engine; Jhoira's ETB+attack value is maximized by exactly that engine.

weakest_slots.weakness: Always-tapped tri-land slows the turn-4/5 commander and double-pip spells.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Nesting Grounds adds sorcery-speed finality relocation but is colorless; fixing loss in a UU/BB/RR deck outweighs it (RETAIN_ALTERNATIVE).

weakest_slots.weakness: Third two-mana BR rock in an eight-rock suite; low ceiling after turn three.
weakest_slots.reasoning: A free sacrifice outlet only pays off with stolen creatures or counter-removed Pirates; the rock is the more reliable commander-on-curve card (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Three-mana lord + one Treasure; as a Brass return its anthem does not include itself.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Ravager's symmetric one-third life loss also hits this life-paying deck (shocks, Talismans, BMC, Vampiric, Reanimate, Confluence); lord + mana is steadier (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Five-mana; Vehicle clause nearly blank (only The Indomitable); value is end-step Treasures from tapped Pirates.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Crew's threaten activation costs {3}{R} per use and lacks a free sac outlet; Kenway's Treasure output after an alpha strike is larger (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana; value depends on a stream of Pirate entries.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Raiders locks a blocker on every Brass return (each return is a Pirate entering) and channels as removal; Copy is a clone whose value depends on the board (REJECT).

weakest_slots.weakness: Symmetric: every opponent returns their own chosen type.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Back in Town is one-sided but X-costed and returns only outlaws for {X}{2}{B}; Bidding returns all Pirates for five and also hits changeling tokens; retained.

weakest_slots.weakness: Card disadvantage; its value is only discarding Pirates for Brass.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Big Score is card-neutral plus two Treasures but costs four; one-mana pre-combat enabling on turn 5 (Brass + Looting) is unique; retained.

weakest_slots.weakness: Two-mana artifact that does nothing alone.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Conduit is instant-speed and not a creature (no summoning-sickness delay), so the finality counter can be removed the same combat the Pirate returns; Diviner needs a full turn cycle and dies to sweepers; retained.

weakest_slots.weakness: Boast sacrifice only once per turn and only after attacking.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Bombardiers is a sac outlet that converts the sacrificed permanent into 2+MV damage; Pit is a free outlet that does nothing alone; retained.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: The approved Oct 13 list is coherent and already strong: it fixed the older Proposed_Final by adding Mary Read and Anne Bonny, Brass's Tunnel-Grinder and Power Conduit and dropping Windfall/Ghost of Ramirez. Its weakness is a handful of low-ceiling two-drop Pirates and one death-trigger card that the finality counter disables.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: Historical pool (Soul Diviner, Grim Captain's Locker, Back in Town, Arm-Mounted Anchor, Port of Karfell, Nephalia Drownyard, Warkite Marauder, Kitesail Larcenist, Dire Fleet Ravager, Nesting Grounds); EDHREC all-decks and optimized commander pages (2026-10-23); a full frozen-cache Oracle scan of 140 commander-legal UBR Pirate creatures not in the list; plus a targeted scan for free sacrifice outlets, counter movers, extra combats and all-types enablers.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: OFF-RANKING search found Jhoira, Weatherlight Corsair (EDHREC New Cards only, 6/21 optimized decks) — selected — and confirmed Ashnod's Altar, Spawning Pit, Maskwood Nexus and Karlach as plausible but rejected. Nephalia Drownyard was not material (colorless slow mill competes with a colored land slot).

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Five one-for-one commander-first upgrades, each replacing a low-ceiling Pirate with a Pirate whose ETB/attack trigger Brass multiplies: repeatable multiplayer removal (Larcenist), per-attack blocker neutralization (Warkite), extra turns from a hasty return (Navigator), early Treasure/card tempo (Ragavan) and a premium reanimation value target (Jhoira). Pirate count, land count and curve are preserved; lost roles (conditional Treasure, explore, 2/2 tokens, unblockable 1-drop, death-trigger Treasure) are all redundant or anti-synergistic with finality counters.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: After the five swaps all remaining 99 slots were re-challenged: lands (Crumbling Necropolis vs Nesting Grounds/Port of Karfell), rocks (Talismans/Signets vs Ashnod's Altar, Spawning Pit, Herald's Horn), Pirates (Corsair Captain vs Dire Fleet Ravager, Edward Kenway vs Captivating Crew/Karlach, Merchant Raiders vs Pirated Copy, Dire Fleet Daredevil vs Glint-Horn Buccaneer), spells (Faithless Looting vs Big Score/Windfall, Patriarch's Bidding vs Back in Town), engines (Power Conduit vs Soul Diviner, Kindred Discovery vs Maskwood Nexus, Lightning Greaves vs Grim Captain's Locker).

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: SELF-CHALLENGE #1. Sorcery-speed only ({1},{T}): it can strip the finality counter from a Brass-returned Pirate only in main phase 2 or later, whereas instant-speed Power Conduit can answer removal in response. It produces only {C}, cutting U/B/R sources from 26/24/24 to 25/23/23 while the five adds raise blue pips from 24 to 27. Not a clear win, so it stays a retained alternative (six-swap file).

SELF-CHALLENGE #2. The Altar nets mana only by sacrificing creatures. A Brass-returned Pirate is exiled by finality, Pitiless Plunderer is cut (no Treasure loop), and Bombardiers/Victimize already supply outlets. Talisman of Indulgence is a turn-2 B/R source that enables a turn-4 five-mana Brass. The Altar wins only with stolen creatures, so this is a REJECT.
Symmetric one-third life loss also taxes our own life-paying mana and tutors; the lord+Treasure three-drop is steadier.
Mana-costed sorcery threaten duplicates Coercive Recruiter's free steals; Kenway's end-step Treasures fund recasts.
Pit needs Power Conduit or a stolen creature to matter and makes no mana; sacrificing a finality Pirate exiles it.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: The six-swap self-challenge: a land slot that can move a finality counter off the best returned ETB Pirate so it can be bounced or recurred again later.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Sorcery-speed only, duplicates instant-speed Power Conduit, and turns a three-color land into a colorless one when blue demand has just gone up. Not clearly better.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Adds a counter-movement and free-sacrifice loop so the single best ETB Pirate can be reused every turn and stolen creatures can be permanently sacrificed.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Both extra cards are conditional on other pieces; they cost a three-color land and a reliable rock, weakening turn-4 Brass more than the loop gains.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: More aggression and theft: Ravager's life-total cut each return, repeatable threaten, and a free outlet for stolen creatures.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Self-damage, redundancy with Coercive Recruiter and the weakest free outlet; none clearly beats the incumbent it replaces.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: Stopped because the next-best outside candidates (Nesting Grounds, Ashnod's Altar, Dire Fleet Ravager, Captivating Crew, Spawning Pit, Pirated Copy) no longer clearly beat a plausible incumbent once their conditional dependencies, fixing cost or self-damage are counted; adding them would be padding, not improvement. Explicit self-challenge on the exact five: the two strongest remaining outsiders are Nesting Grounds (vs Crumbling Necropolis) and Ashnod's Altar (vs Talisman of Indulgence). Both were built as full 100-card files (six- and seven-swap) and both lose concretely: sorcery-speed colorless land vs a three-color source, and a conditional free outlet vs a turn-4-Brass rock. Neither was added.
